issues.title: issues from Will L's review
issues.author: gmarzot
issues.body:
Just some minor points I noted:

"Tuple fields that precede field 0 are a prefix chosen by the deployment." - how can there be a tuple field lower than 0 ?

"Catalog cmsf requires cmaf or locmaf." - since CMSF extends MSF, it supports everything that MSF supports, so "loc" should also be allowed. 

Why H.264 Constrained Baseline? H.264 High profile is supported by nearly all devices?

"The publisher publishes the following tracks in the Track Namespace:" - wouldn;t catalog, audio and video be track names rather than namespaces? Catalog is defined as a reserved track name. 

You don;t provide options for how init data is carried (in the catalog, as a track property or as a Object property. Is this intentional?

comments.author: gmarzot
comments.body:
All five points are addressed in #4, now in the [editor's copy](https://gmarzot.github.io/draft-marzot-moq-test-tracks/draft-marzot-moq-test-tracks.html):

1. **Fields before field 0.** Reworded: a namespace can begin with a prefix of fields the deployment chooses, and the defined tuple fields follow it, numbered from 0.
2. **cmsf with loc.** Catalog (Tuple Field 1) is now `msf | none`. A CMSF catalog carries no marker of its own, so `cmsf` with `loc` would name the same catalog as `msf` with `loc`. `msf` now means an MSF catalog that uses the CMSF extensions for cmaf and locmaf tracks.
3. **H.264 profile.** `h264` is H.264 High. `h264cb` is Constrained Baseline, kept for constrained devices.
4. **Track names.** The section is now "Track Names". `catalog` is the name MSF reserves; `video` and `audio` are defined here.
5. **Init data.** New Tuple Field 3: `catalog | track | object`, mapped to MSF's Initialization Data List types (inline, track-property, object-property). cmaf and locmaf use `catalog`, as CMSF requires; with no catalog the field is `_`. Later fields are renumbered; Duration is now Field 16.

The service follows the same encoding in openmoq/moq-test-tracks#11, deployed at moq-test.ci.openmoq.org.

pulls.title: Carry wall-clock capture time via timestamp mapping
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
Adds latency timing to the test tracks without a new tuple field and without per-object bytes on schedule.

- **Tracks → Timing (new subsection).** Every media track carries the TIMESCALE and TIMESTAMP_MAPPING Track Properties of draft-frindell-moq-timestamp, without CLOCK_ID, so timestamps are wall-clock time. Video timescale is 1000 × fps (24000/30000/60000 for the fractional rates, Object Multiplier 1001); audio timescale is the sample rate with the Object Multiplier set to samples per frame. Off-schedule objects carry an OBJECT_TIMESTAMP correction.
- **LOC:** the Timestamp property is the capture time in µs since the Unix epoch; the LOC Timescale property is not sent.
- **CMAF / LOCMAF:** a prft box in the first object of each group.
- **Tuple Field 7:** the group duration must be a whole number of frames, so the mapping is exact.
- **Latency:** one paragraph defining latency and noting that it needs agreeing clocks (co-located subscriber, or a common time source).
- **References:** draft-frindell-moq-timestamp added as normative.

Considered and left out: an MSF media timeline track (it serves seeking, has ms resolution and a separate subscription) and an in-band clock-offset track.

Verified: i-d-template `make` and `make lint` pass.

pulls.title: Drop audio sample rate field, pcm and vp9
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
Stacked on #1. Cuts knobs that don't serve the conformance and performance goals of the test tracks.

- **Tuple Field 10 (Audio Sample Rate) removed.** Audio is always 48000 Hz. Fields 11–16 become 10–15, so a namespace has 16 tuple fields in all. The audio timescale in Timing is 48000.
- **`pcm` removed** from Tuple Field 9: the target players can't decode it, and only one tool emits it.
- **`vp9` removed** from Tuple Field 3: rare in MoQ deployments.
- Examples, the §8.8 rendering, and the field cross-references (none ⇒ fields 10–13 are `_`, duration in field 15) are updated.

Verified: i-d-template `make` and `make lint` pass, and every example has 15 fields after the version tuple.

pulls.title: Add clip content value
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
Adds `clip` to Tuple Field 14 (Content): natural content, such as a film, chosen by the publisher and encoded to the namespace's parameters. Synthetic patterns cannot stand in for real scene complexity, but the draft does not name any clip: which clip a deployment offers is a publisher choice, expressed in the Track Namespace prefix.

pulls.title: Address review: catalog, init data, H.264 profile, wording
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
Responds to Will Law's comments on the editor's copy.

1. **Prefix wording.** "Tuple fields that precede field 0" read as a field numbered below 0. Now: a namespace can begin with a prefix of deployment-chosen fields, and the defined tuple fields follow it, numbered from 0. Exactly 17 tuple fields after the prefix.
2. **Catalog (Tuple Field 1): `msf | none`.** CMSF extends MSF, including LOC support, and a CMSF catalog carries no marker of its own (same `version`). `cmsf`+`loc` would have named the same catalog as `msf`+`loc`. `msf` now means an MSF catalog using the CMSF extensions for cmaf and locmaf tracks. Valid pairs: msf with loc, cmaf or locmaf; none with loc.
3. **H.264 profile (Tuple Field 4).** `h264` = High, `h264cb` = Constrained Baseline; still no B-frames, lowest fitting level.
4. **Track Names.** The Tracks section now says these are Track Names under the namespace. `catalog` is the name MSF reserves; `video` and `audio` are defined here.
5. **Init Data (new Tuple Field 3): `catalog | track | object`.** These map to MSF's Initialization Data List entry types: inline, track-property (VIDEO_CONFIG / AUDIO_CONFIG Track Property) and object-property (the same on the first object of each group). The last two are in the MSF editor's copy, now an informative reference. cmaf and locmaf use `catalog`, as CMSF requires for CMAF headers. Without a catalog the field is `_` and init data is in band.

Later fields renumber (Video Codec is now 4 … Duration 16). Examples updated, including one each for `track` and `object` with `h264cb`.

Verified: i-d-template `make` and `make lint` pass, and every example has 16 fields after the version.

pulls.title: Content classes, publisher-chosen clips and clip discovery
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
Tuple Field 15 names content by what it lets a subscriber measure, and leaves the choice of real media to each deployment.

- **`ts` → `clock`.** The picture **must** show the capture time of each frame; it was a SHOULD. The group and object IDs stay SHOULD.
- **`clip` is publisher-chosen content.** The document specifies no clip. Each deployment chooses its own clips and may add to them. The last field of the Track Namespace prefix identifies the clip, and the prefix bullet in "Track Namespace Parameters" now names that one exception to "not interpreted". The picture SHOULD carry any attribution a clip's licence requires.
- **Discovery.** An on-demand publisher sends one PUBLISH_NAMESPACE per clip, with the clip's prefix, so SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE on the deployment's prefix lists the clips. No new mechanism.
- **Extension stays through `clip`.** The defined values remain a closed set, so a test name always has a defined meaning, and an unknown value is still DOES_NOT_EXIST. That avoids an `x_`-style private range (RFC 6648).
- **Examples** use `clock`, plus a clip example with the neutral id `clip_a`. No real source names appear in the document.

The service follows in openmoq/moq-test-tracks#16.

The i-d-template tools aren't installed on my machine, so the build and lint for this change are this repo's CI.

pulls.title: Capture time is before encoding
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
The Timing section said capture time is when "the publisher produced the frame", which is ambiguous between before and after encoding. On the same path, moq-test-tracks measured about 28 ms for live-encoded LOC and about 2 ms for pre-encoded CMAF loops.

- **Capture time:** the wall-clock time at which the frame is captured, before encoding. A publisher sending recorded (pre-encoded) media uses each frame's scheduled time.
- **Latency:** it includes encoding only when the publisher encodes live, so latency results state how the media was encoded.

pulls.title: Fix target latency at 250 ms
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
Every track in the MSF catalog is live and carries `targetLatency` 250 ms. No tuple field sets it.

The target tells the player how far behind live to render. It describes neither the media nor how it is delivered, so varying it changes nothing a relay, transport or publisher test measures. Fixing it keeps every catalog field determined by the test name, and a player test that needs another target can set it in the player. 250 ms rather than 200 ms: players underran at 200 ms.

The service side is openmoq/moq-test-tracks#33.

pulls.title: Rework the tuple fields: required first, optional trailing, video tracks
pulls.author: gmarzot
pulls.body:
This revises the `moq_test_tracks_00` tuple fields in place (the draft has not been submitted yet). It has three goals: shorter names for the common cases, a namespace that stays focused on format compatibility and rendering, and a way to request more than one video track (bitrate ladders and multiple views) for switching tests.

## What changes

**Order and optional fields.** Required fields come first. Tuning fields follow, and a name may stop after any field from 8 onward. Each omitted field takes the value its section gives, or `_` where it does not apply.

| # | Field | When omitted |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `moq_test_tracks_00` | required |
| 1 | content (clock, bars, noise, clip) | required |
| 2 | catalog (msf, none) | required |
| 3 | packaging (loc, cmaf, locmaf) | required |
| 4 | video codec | required |
| 5 | video height | required |
| 6 | frame rate | required |
| 7 | audio codec | required |
| 8 | audio channels | required |
| 9 | init data | catalog |
| 10 | group duration | 2000, or 2002 at 23_976, 29_97, 59_94 |
| 11 | audio delivery: `1`–`100` frames per group, or `dgram` | 1 |
| 12 | duration | 0 |
| 13 | video tracks (new) | 1 |

Names that differ only in omitted fields describe the same tracks. A publisher names a set of tracks with the shortest form.

**Forwarding preferences are gone.** Every group goes on one stream as subgroup 0, following MSF §6 as revised by [moq-wg/msf#169](https://github.com/moq-wg/msf/pull/169). Nobody sends video one stream per frame or in datagrams. For audio, the one remaining choice is streams or datagrams, so the audio frames per group field becomes Audio Delivery: `1`–`100` frames per group on streams, or `dgram`, where each frame is its own group in a datagram. Per-object stream mappings remain testable with synthetic objects in moq-test.

**Bitrates are no longer fields.** The video bitrate follows from height (a table, 1.5 times above 30 fps), and the audio bitrate from codec and channels. The main audience tests format compatibility and rendering, where bitrate rarely matters. Bandwidth and load testing is better served by moq-test's explicit object sizes. A side effect is that every set of tracks stays within the codec level its height and frame rate imply.

**Video Tracks (field 13).**
- `alt2` to `alt7` is a ladder. Each rendition takes the largest defined height at most three quarters of the one before it, and the table bitrate for its height. For example, `alt3` at 1080p gives 1080, 720 and 540.
- `view2` to `view16` gives N views at the same height and frame rate.
- The Track Names are `video`, `video_1`, `video_2` and so on.
- Every video track has a catalog label. A ladder shares one altGroup; each view has its own.
- Group IDs and Object IDs line up across the video tracks, so a switch at any group boundary is seamless.

**Also.**
- Publisher Behavior now describes both delivery modes: PUBLISH for each track, or PUBLISH_NAMESPACE only, with the relay forwarding SUBSCRIBEs.
- It notes that a short name is a tuple prefix of its longer variants, which affects prefix routing and SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE.
- Security Considerations adds the number of video tracks to the limits, and cites CAT for MOQT ([draft-ietf-moq-c4m](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-moq-c4m/)) as an example of relay authorization for on-demand publishers.

## Before and after

| Set of tracks | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 720p30 H.264, stereo AAC | `msf/loc/catalog/h264/720/30/2500/2000/0/aac/2/128/1/0/clock/0` | `clock/msf/loc/h264/720/30/aac/2` |
| init data on each group's first object | `msf/loc/object/h264cb/360/30/600/2000/0/aac/2/128/1/0/clock/0` | `clock/msf/loc/h264cb/360/30/aac/2/object` |
| clip, 1080p30 CMAF | `msf/cmaf/catalog/h264/1080/30/4500/2000/0/aac/2/128/1/0/clip/0` | `clip/msf/cmaf/h264/1080/30/aac/2` |
| AV1 + Opus over datagrams | `msf/loc/track/av1/1080/60/6000/2000/0/opus/2/64/1/3/clock/0` | `clock/msf/loc/av1/1080/60/opus/2/track/2000/dgram` |
| 3-rendition ladder | (not expressible) | `clock/msf/loc/h264/1080/30/aac/2/catalog/2000/1/0/alt3` |

All after `<prefix>/moq_test_tracks_00/`.

## Questions for review

1. Are two names for one set of tracks acceptable, given that the shortest form is the one publishers use? Relays treat them as different namespaces.
2. Do any compatibility tests need bitrate as an explicit field? If so, it could come back as an optional trailing field.
3. Is a fixed ladder rule right for a test spec, or should the namespace list each rendition?
4. Index Track Names (`video_1`), or descriptive ones (`video_720p`)? Index names also work for views, and keep `video` for players that only know one track.
5. Views each get their own altGroup. Is there a use for renderGroup (views rendered together), or is that out of scope?
6. Within the optional fields, the order goes from the most to the least often varied. Does it match what you would vary?
7. Is datagram audio with one frame per group enough, or does anyone send several frames per group in datagrams? A `dgramN` value could be added later.
